standard_prerequisites.name: Conditions, stabilisation, the limit colouring and the three lemmas of the section
standard_prerequisites.statement: A condition is a triple of a colouring constrained by a computable bounding function, a finite stem and an infinite reservoir computing a fixed set D, subject to the defining properties (a) and (b) about how the images of finite sets meet the stem and the reservoir; a reservoir stabilises an interval when the images of its finite sets land in fixed finite sets of short tuples, and the section attaches a limit colouring to such a reservoir. Three lemmas of the same section, stated and proved earlier at source lines 1121-1133, 1144-1150 and 1162-1175, provide respectively a reservoir preserving property (a), a reservoir stabilising the stem, and the preservation of property (b) when a free block is appended to the stem. The author's own definitions and those three lemmas are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the extensibility statement that drives the generic filter construction of the section: starting from any condition it produces one with a strictly longer stem while keeping the defining properties, and the three lemmas are exactly the tools it combines.

core_obligations: Take the least element of the reservoir and stabilise the interval up to it: the stabilising lemma of the section supplies an infinite subset of the reservoir that stabilises the interval from zero to that element and still avoids the cone of the fixed set, which is the first step towards appending that element to the stem (source line 1183, first sentence).

Recover property (a) for the enlarged stem: applying the lemma that preserves property (a) by shrinking the reservoir once more yields an infinite subset of the stabilised set for which the condition whose stem is the old stem together with the least reservoir element satisfies property (a) (source line 1183, second sentence).

Recover property (b): the added block is a single element, hence vacuously free for the limit colouring, so the lemma that appends a free block to the stem applies and gives that the same enlarged triple satisfies property (b) as well; together with the untouched properties (c) and the reservoir inclusion this makes the enlarged triple an extension with a strictly longer stem (source line 1184).

proof_roadmap.step: Stabilise the interval up to the least reservoir element and keep the cone avoided.
Shrink the reservoir once more to restore property (a) for the enlarged stem.
Append the element as a vacuous free block to restore property (b) and read off the extension.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的 Lemma lem:fs-extendibility（源 1179-1181 行，证明 1182-1185 行）：对任意 condition (f,σ,X)，存在扩张 (f,τ,Y) ≤ (f,σ,X) 使 |τ| > |σ|。关键操作不是例行核验：证明要把**三条**同章引理按正确顺序接起来——先取 x=min X，用 stabilize 引理得到稳定 [0,x] 且保持 D 的锥被避开的 Y₀（1183 行前句）；再对 Y₀ 用 property (a) 保持引理收缩得到 Y，使 (f, σ∪{x}, Y) 满足性质 (a)（1183 行后句）；最后因为加入的块 {x} 对极限着色**空真**（vacuously）free，用 property (b) 保持引理得到 (f, σ∪{x}, Y) 也满足性质 (b)（1184 行）。难点在于「先稳定、再恢复 (a)、再恢复 (b)」这条顺序不可交换，且最后一步必须识别出单元素块的 free 性是空真的；原文位置在证明的 1183、1184 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma lem:fs-extendibility at source lines 1179-1181 together with its proof at source lines 1182-1185, a straight adjacent pairing in the pinned file. The pinned file is a concatenation of the authors' main and macro files; it is the article's fixed version arXiv:2412.11598v3 under CC BY 4.0.

This source ships no separate preamble file, so the retained preamble is sliced mechanically from the pinned file by the lane and is shared, byte for byte, with the other cards of this source; it carries the authors' full macro block and the cleveref package that the retained proof needs for its capitalised cross-references.

Two context spans carry the material the retained statement and proof rely on: the definition of a condition with its properties (a), (b), (c) and the extension relation at lines 1105-1117, and the definition of the limit colouring at lines 1154-1156. Both are context, not counted units, and neither overlaps the counted interval.

The retained proof names three lemmas of the same section at source lines 1121-1125, 1144-1147 and 1162-1167, each of which is counted by a separate card of this lane. All three are declared as non-load-bearing navigation pointers with the article's own section-wise numbers 6.16, 6.18 and 6.20, counted over the numbered environments of section 6; none of their statements is reproduced inside the span, and no bibliography is needed because the retained spans contain no citation.

The proof leans on the defining property (c) of a condition and on the reservoir inclusion only implicitly, through the word extension; the retained context supplies both, so the card does not depend on material outside its own spans apart from the three pointers.
